# jibo-ota-updater

Set of tools used to find, download, and apply OTA updates.

Canonically, the OTA update process consists of 3 phases: Getting the update metadata, downloading the update, and applying the update. Here's an example:
```
# jibo-get-update --credentials /var/jibo/credentials.json --subsystem services --version 0.11.2
{"_id":"56ec1391816b110a00044429","length":1536,"shaHash":"7c884560da82226e8cfa43a75e64e8a194e2e7dc","url":"http://s3.amazonaws.com/update.jibo.com/56ec1391816b110a00044429","subsystem":"services","dependencies":{"os":"0.11.3"},"changes":"all the things","toVersion":"0.11.3","fromVersion":"0.11.2","created":1458312081620,"accountId":"56ea9ef7197d3e09000c3181"}
# jibo-download-update --url http://s3.amazonaws.com/update.jibo.com/56ec1391816b110a00044429 --destination /opt/ota/0.11.3-services.tar --shasum 7c884560da82226e8cfa43a75e64e8a194e2e7dc
{"length":1536,"received":0,"status":"initialized"}
{"length":1536,"received":1536,"status":"downloading"}
{"length":1536,"received":1536,"status":"finished"}
# DISPLAY=:0 XAUTHORITY=/tmp/.Xauthority jibo-apply-update --source /opt/ota/0.11.3-services.tar --subsystem services --from 0.11.2 --to 0.11.3
(GUI shown... system reboots...)
```

## jibo-list-updates

Command line utility to list any available updates for a subsystem.

## jibo-get-update

Command line utility to get the best available update for a subsystem from a given version.

## jibo-download-update

Command line utility to download an update from a provided URL and verify its checksum.

## jibo-apply-update

Does the grunt work of extracting and applying a downloaded update. Draws a simple X11 GUI to indicate progress.

## Update Package Format

The overall package is an uncompressed tarball. It contains the following:

```
gordon@jgw-mbp:~/Sandboxes/jibo-updater$ tar tf 0.11.3-services.tar 
./
./filesystem.tar.bz2
./postinstall
./preinstall
```

All three are OPTIONAL. You could potentially have an update in which the package is extracted, no further action is taken, and success is declared. Why you would want this, I don’t know, but you can do it.

The preinstall and postinstall scripts are launched in the directory where we extracted the update, and it is not illegal to put additional files in the update package, so potentially they could do all kinds of crazy things. We should avoid ever doing that, but its nice to have the hook. An error status reported by either preinstall or postinstall is considered a fatal error, and the update will be redownloaded and retried.

## Managing Update Packages for Testing

### Create OS/Services packages from buildroot build artifacts
```
sudo node src/package-update.js --image /path/to/output/images/rootfs.ext4 --subsystem os --outfile os_pkg.tar
sudo node src/package-update.js --image /path/to/output/images/services.ext4 --subsystem services --outfile services_pkg.tar
```

### Create skill package from repository artifacts
```
wget http://repository.jibo.com/sdk/path/to/skill.tar.gz
mkdir tmp
tar -C tmp/ -xf skill.tar.gz --strip 1
tar -C tmp/ -cjf filesystem.tar.bz2 .
rm -rf tmp
mkdir tmp
mv filesystem.tar.bz2 tmp/
tar -C tmp/ -cf skill-pkg.tar .
```

### Upload a package to the cloud
```
node src/create-update.js --credentials /path/to/credentials-admin.json --subsystem os --file os_pkg.tar --from 0.11.1 --to 0.11.2 --depends '{}' --changes "cool os stuff"
node src/create-update.js --credentials /path/to/credentials-admin.json --subsystem services --file services_pkg.tar --from 0.11.1 --to 0.11.2 --depends '{"os":"0.11.2"}' --changes "cool services stuff"

```

### Remove a package from the cloud
```
node src/remove-update.js --credentials /path/to/credentials-admin.json --subsystem os --id <id to remove>
```
